posts.subject: IdeaPad Gaming 3 15IHU6 — HDMI port stopped working mid-use, cannot use monitor above 60hz
posts.author: asisqt
posts.message_html:
I own a Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 15IHU6 (82K1) with Intel Core i5 11th Gen, NVIDIA RTX 3050, 16GB RAM, running Windows 11 Home.

I recently purchased a Lenovo Legion 24-10 240Hz monitor and connected it via HDMI. I discovered that the HDMI port on this laptop is hardwired to the Intel Iris Xe integrated GPU, not the dedicated RTX 3050. This means I am completely unable to use my Legion 24-10 at its rated 240Hz — I am locked to 60Hz maximum.

Here is the full timeline of what happened:

I was actively using my monitor — watching a show — when the HDMI port suddenly stopped outputting any signal completely without any warning. No physical damage occurred, no cable was moved or disturbed. It just stopped working mid-session.

I initially suspected the monitor was faulty, so I raised a warranty claim with Lenovo. My Legion 24-10 was replaced under warranty. However, even with the brand new replacement monitor, the HDMI port still does not output any signal. This confirms the issue is with the laptop's HDMI port, not the monitor.

Issues I was facing even before the port stopped working:

Locked to 60Hz — unable to use the Legion 24-10 at its rated 240Hz due to HDMI being hardwired to Intel Iris Xe

Random blackouts — monitor would occasionally lose signal and go blank before recovering

Laggy video playback — 60fps video content played with noticeable frame drops on the external monitor

All software fixes I have already tried:

Updated Intel Iris Xe drivers via Device Manager

Updated NVIDIA RTX 3050 drivers manually from NVIDIA website

Ran Lenovo Vantage System Update

Checked Display Settings — Windows detects the monitor under Monitors in Device Manager

Intel Graphics Command Center fully detects the Legion 24-10 as connected via HDMI — but no signal is output to the monitor

Tested with multiple HDMI cables

Tested both HDMI ports on the monitor

Performed full laptop restart and shutdown cycles with monitor connected

Tried Windows + P display switching options

Despite all of the above, the monitor shows "Not Connected" and receives no signal.

A local Lenovo authorized service centre has quoted ₹25,000 for a full motherboard replacement, which seems disproportionate for what appears to be an isolated HDMI port failure.

My questions:

Is the HDMI port on the 15IHU6 truly soldered onto the motherboard with no component-level repair possible?

Has anyone experienced sudden HDMI port failure on this model mid-use?

Is there any BIOS setting or firmware fix that could restore HDMI output?

Is there any way to route display output through the RTX 3050 instead of Intel Iris Xe on this model?

Can Lenovo offer any support or goodwill repair given this is a known hardware limitation of this model?

System Details:

Model: Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 15IHU6 (82K1)

CPU: Intel Core i5 11th Gen

GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3050 + Intel Iris Xe (Optimus)

RAM: 16GB

OS: Windows 11 Home

Monitor: Lenovo Legion 24-10 (240Hz) — replaced under warranty, issue persists

Connection: HDMI

Any help from the community or Lenovo support is greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

posts.subject: Re:IdeaPad Gaming 3 15IHU6 — HDMI port stopped working mid-use, cannot use monitor above 60hz
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hi and welcome to the Lenovo Community asisqt,

Thanks for the detailed breakdown—very helpful. I’ll address your points and share the quickest next steps.

Key design notes for IdeaPad Gaming 3 15IHU6 (82K1) - On most configs the HDMI port is routed through the Intel iGPU. There’s no MUX or BIOS option to force the HDMI output through the RTX 3050 on this platform. - The maximum external refresh rate over HDMI depends on the HDMI version implemented on your exact sub-model and firmware. You can check its specifications by clicking here.

About the sudden HDMI failure mid-use - Given Windows/Intel GCC can detect the monitor (EDID present) but the screen shows no image, it can be a signal/handshake path issue (e.g., level shifter/retimer/port hardware) or firmware/driver state. - A quick way to separate OS vs. hardware: connect the monitor and try entering BIOS (F2/F1 on boot). If there’s still no image on the external display even before Windows loads, that strongly suggests a hardware issue.

Try these steps (in order)

1) Full power/EC reset - Shut down the laptop completely. - Unplug AC and any peripherals. - Hold the power button for 60 seconds. - Reconnect AC only, then boot and test HDMI.

2) BIOS defaults and updates - Enter BIOS (F2/F1) > Load Setup Defaults > Save & Exit. - Update BIOS/firmware via Lenovo Vantage System Update or your product page on Lenovo Support.

3) Clean reinstall Intel graphics - Uninstall Intel Graphics in Device Manager (check “Delete the driver software for this device”). Reboot. - Install the Lenovo-recommended Intel graphics package from your support page (preferred), or use Intel’s driver after testing Lenovo’s. Then reinstall NVIDIA and run Windows Update/Vantage again.

4) HDMI handshake checks - Test different power-on order: boot to Windows first, then plug HDMI; also try plugging before power on. - In Intel Graphics Command Center, set 1920×1080 at 60Hz first, disable HDR, set 8-bit color to test. - Disable Windows Fast Startup (Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do). - If possible, test the laptop with a different display or TV to confirm behavior.

Regarding 60Hz limit and higher refresh options - On this model, HDMI is routed via the Intel iGPU and may be limited by the port version/firmware. If your specific 15IHU6 configuration supports USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, you can often achieve higher refresh rates by using a USB-C to DisplayPort cable directly to the monitor’s DP input. If your USB-C does not support DP Alt Mode, a USB graphics (DisplayLink) adapter can be a functional workaround for desktop use, but it’s not ideal for gaming due to added latency and potential frame drops.

Service/repair expectations - The HDMI connector and its associated circuitry are part of the system board. Lenovo-authorized repairs do not perform micro-solder/component-level fixes; the standard remedy is system board replacement. - If BIOS/driver resets don’t restore output (and no pre-OS image is shown), service is likely required. You can: - Check warranty and options: Warranty Status - Submit a ticket: Service Request - Or locate another Authorized Service Center for a second opinion/quote: Authorized Service Centers - For out-of-warranty, you may ask about depot flat-rate repair if available in your region. You can contact technical support at 1800-419-7555 / 1800-121-5366(Tata Subscribers) and their operating hours are Monday to Saturday 9:00 AM to 18:00 PM IST.

Answers to your specific questions:

Is HDMI soldered/no component-level repair? Yes—the port is on the system board; Lenovo’s repair procedure is board replacement rather than port-only repair. -

Sudden HDMI failure mid-use seen before? It can occur, though it’s not common. Your symptoms (EDID detected, no image) align with a hardware signaling fault or a persistent firmware state—hence the reset/update steps above.

Any BIOS/firmware setting to restore HDMI? No specific switch for HDMI routing; try BIOS update and Load Defaults as above. If no output even in BIOS, it points to hardware.

Route output through RTX 3050 instead of Intel? Not on this model; there’s no MUX/“dGPU only” mode for the HDMI port.

Goodwill repair/support? Please contact our support team still with your case history and the monitor replacement details—regional teams can review options based on warranty status and service policies.

Hope this helps. Please let us know if you have any other concerns or questions.

Best regards,
Adriel_Lenovo
